edges.effect_quant: A Cochrane review of ulcerative colitis remission maintenance found no relapse benefit with fish oil (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.51-2.03), and the large EPIC Crohn disease trials were likewise negative.
edges.population: adults with quiescent ulcerative colitis or Crohn disease in clinical remission
edges.mechanism: Omega-3 fatty acids can alter eicosanoid balance and theoretically dampen mucosal inflammation, but that biochemical plausibility has not translated into consistent remission maintenance in clinical trials. The most likely interpretation is that any anti-inflammatory effect is too small or too formulation-dependent to reliably prevent relapse in established IBD.
edges.summary: Omega-3 supplementation has not shown a dependable ability to maintain remission in IBD. Both older ulcerative colitis trials and the large EPIC Crohn disease studies failed to demonstrate a meaningful relapse-prevention benefit, making the most defensible conclusion a neutral one rather than an encouraging but underpowered positive signal.
edges.caveats: These trials used different formulations and may not resolve whether specific enteric or higher-dose preparations help selected subgroups. Still, the burden of evidence currently argues against routine omega-3 supplementation as a reliable remission-maintenance strategy.

evidence.citation: Turner D et al 2007 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
